about: Cabernet Sauvignon is a gamble in a climate as cool as the Finger Lakes, which makes it a fitting grape for Dr. Konstantin Frank Winery. Its founder, a Ukrainian viticulturist with a doctorate in growing grapes in cold places, arrived in New York in 1951 and spent his career arguing that European vinifera could thrive here. He planted his first vineyard on Keuka Lake in 1958 and released his first wines in 1962. The winery is still run by his family, now in its fourth generation.

The 2023 draws on two estates: Keuka Lake vines planted in 1974 and 1997, and, for most of the blend, Seneca Lake vineyards in the warmer “Banana Belt.” A severe mid-May freeze took 10 to 50 percent of the buds, concentrating the crop that remained. The grapes were destemmed, cold-soaked for several days and fermented in temperature-controlled open-top stainless steel with twice-daily pumpovers, then aged 16 months in French oak, 20 percent of it new.

The winemakers describe a deep ruby wine with black cherry, blackberry and fig, florals, dried herbs and a touch of green peppercorn, plus cedar and spice from the barrel. The palate is fruit-forward but structured, with grippy tannins and bright acidity, and finishes on dark fruit, leather and earth: a lighter, fresher take on Cabernet than warmer regions produce.
facts: Cold soak; open-top stainless steel fermentation, twice-daily pumpovers
